children: FAW, maker of Chairman Mao’s favourite limo, is set to become a top shareholder of $6.4 bln GAC. A tie-up could end competition between the state automakers' Toyota ventures and stem losses. Rising trade barriers overseas strengthen the case to shutter unneeded factories at home.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Katrina Hamlin on Bluesky and Linkedin.
Shanghai-listed Guangzhou Automobile Group (GAC) intends to acquire part of FAW's stake in a vehicle-manufacturing joint venture, GAC said in a statement on September 14.
GAC intends to issue A-shares to fund the transaction. If completed, FAW is expected to become ​GAC's second-largest shareholder with strategic influence, GAC added.
GAC’s Hong Kong-listed shares rose as much as 8% in morning trade on September 15. Its Shanghai shares were suspended.
FAW group’s core passenger-vehicle business is not listed.
